incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS customers (internet-exposed management interfaces)
incidents.vector: Attackers chained the critical PHP2Shell remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug to gain root access on PAN-OS management interfaces left exposed to the internet.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed active exploitation achieving root access on affected firewalls; over 22.6 million PHP instances worldwide remain potentially exposed, though patched/non-exposed systems are unaffected.

incidents.victim: Moldovan government services and citizens
incidents.attacker: Unknown — possible foreign state involvement under investigation
incidents.vector: Hackers exploited an unauthenticated, internet-exposed logging service to make roughly 11 million data-access requests, then pivoted into interconnected government systems to extract records.
incidents.impact: Personal data on about 750,000 citizens (roughly a third of the population) was exposed, including health, financial, and family details; 82 digital services and 30 government networks were taken offline, with repeat intrusion attempts since blocked.

incidents.victim: U.S. critical infrastructure operators (telecom, energy, water, transportation, defense)
incidents.vector: Exploited zero-day and known vulnerabilities in network-edge devices via a constantly rebuilt chain of compromised routers and IoT devices ("Silent Train"), reassembled in under two minutes to minimize detectable infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Sustained covert access to hundreds of victim organizations across telecom, government, defense, water, energy, transportation, maritime, rail, aviation, and emergency-services sectors since late 2023.

incidents.victim: Space/satellite, defense/aerospace, and policy-research organizations
incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controllers, to deploy the custom "KeyDrift" malware framework for persistent, in-memory access to the control plane.
incidents.impact: Gained long-term access allowing interception of decrypted control traffic and theft of encryption keying material at victims whose infrastructure overlaps with the China-linked "Silent Train" access network.

incidents.victim: Starlink satellite internet users (100+ countries)
incidents.vector: An Israeli ad-tech firm, Discover-Tech, won the top bid for ad placements shown to Starlink users and used that position to serve malicious ads delivering zero-click spyware.
incidents.impact: Zero-click spyware was delivered via ads to Starlink users across more than 100 countries, including countries where Starlink service is banned or restricted.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees and contractors
incidents.vector: A hacktivist group calling itself the Department of Peace obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS and passed it to Distributed Denial of Secrets for publication.
incidents.impact: Internal records on more than 41,000 current and former DHS employees and contractors were published, including staff overseeing covert operations and immigration enforcement; the leak site was later taken offline.

incidents.victim: Japan Airlines / Japan Transocean Air customers
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Amadeus IT Group, the third-party provider running Japan Airlines' reservation, ticketing, and check-in systems, and accessed customer reservation data.
incidents.impact: 92,000 customers had names, reservation codes, and flight data exposed; about 2,000 also had passport numbers, frequent-flyer numbers, emails, and phone numbers stolen. Flight operations and card data were not affected.

incidents.victim: U.S. and allied businesses defrauded by DPRK IT-worker schemes
incidents.vector: North Korean operatives used fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and AI-generated personas to secure remote IT jobs at Western companies, then diverted wages through facilitator-run financial networks.
incidents.impact: Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for laundering proceeds that fund DPRK weapons programs; some IT workers also deployed malware and exfiltrated proprietary data from employer networks.

incidents.victim: University of Copenhagen
incidents.vector: Hackers breached a test environment belonging to the university.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 525,000 people was stolen.

incidents.victim: Keystone (cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker) and its customers
incidents.vector: An attacker stole Keystone's device authentication key, which is written into each wallet during assembly and cannot be changed after the fact.
incidents.impact: Keystone is destroying nearly 19,000 devices and has suspended all deliveries, warning the stolen key could be used to build counterfeit wallets with hidden backdoors.

incidents.victim: Convertr (e-commerce platform) and its customers' shoppers
incidents.vector: A suspected Brazilian Magecart-style group breached Convertr through the Plausible open-source analytics platform and injected a credit-card skimmer into its analytics script.
incidents.impact: Shoppers' payment card data was harvested via the skimmer before the compromise was identified by researchers.

incidents.victim: Bitonic (Dutch cryptocurrency platform) customers
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Bitonic's internal systems and modified account login credentials on the backend to take over accounts.
incidents.impact: Three customer accounts were accessed and emptied of Bitcoin.

incidents.victim: Electrum cryptocurrency wallet users
incidents.vector: Malicious Electrum wallet servers exploited a signing bug to trick wallet owners into unknowingly signing fraudulent transactions.
incidents.impact: At least one user lost funds before Electrum patched the flaw; some malicious servers continue exploiting unpatched clients.

incidents.victim: eMudhra Limited (certificate authority) and downstream TLS / code-signing relying parties
incidents.vector: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority private keys (six TLS, two code-signing) were compromised and recoverable, allowing creation of certificates that would appear trusted.
incidents.impact: Microsoft blocked the affected CAs via the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List and removed seven related root certificates from Windows and Edge, cutting off the keys' ability to impersonate sites or sign malware as trusted software.

incidents.victim: ConnectWise Cloud Backup customers (2,250+ Microsoft 365 tenants)
incidents.vector: The threat actor used compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup application credentials, accelerated by the AI-enabled ARTEX penetration-testing framework, to attempt sign-ins to Microsoft 365 tenants at up to 2,900 attempts per minute.
incidents.impact: The group achieved privileged, persistent cloud access at multiple organizations across manufacturing, aerospace, chemicals, energy, defense, and financial services, though most targeting attempts failed.

incidents.victim: Hospitals, law firms, and businesses in the U.S. and abroad
incidents.vector: A ransomware conspiracy involving a Ukrainian national and co-conspirators hacked into hospital, business, and government networks worldwide to deploy ransomware and extort victims.
incidents.impact: Roughly 1,500 victims worldwide were hit, causing over $100 million in losses; the defendant was sentenced to 70 months in prison, though a co-conspirator remains at large.

incidents.victim: Critical infrastructure and manufacturing sites in Spain, France, and U.S. military bases
incidents.vector: Pro-Russian actors exploited internet-connected industrial control and IoT systems — including refrigeration, HVAC, and manufacturing equipment — to trigger physical malfunctions.
incidents.impact: Caused a factory fire at a renewable-energy transformer plant in Catalonia, disrupted winery and crematorium equipment in Spain, and affected supermarket refrigeration in France and systems at U.S. military bases; French and U.S. authorities are investigating jointly.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center
incidents.vector: A new ransomware gang calling itself BYOD compromised internal systems at UNM's hospitals, medical school, and research facilities.
incidents.impact: Ambulances were diverted and outpatient surgeries/appointments canceled for hours; systems were fully restored without paying ransom, though the gang still holds stolen patient and employee data and is attempting to extort individuals directly.

incidents.victim: Vanden Broele (Belgian government software supplier) and 120+ local authorities
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Vanden Broele's eSignFlow document-signing platform, used widely by Belgian local governments.
incidents.impact: More than 120 local authorities were reportedly impacted; the company took systems offline to prevent further abuse.

incidents.victim: Warp (cloud/developer platform) and roughly 1% of its customers
incidents.vector: Intruders used a swarm of AI agents to breach one of Warp's infrastructure suppliers and pivot into Warp's environment.
incidents.impact: Agent trace and telemetry data belonging to roughly 1% of Warp's customers was stolen.

incidents.victim: Blast Mail (email service operated by Laxlight)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached Blast Mail, a Japanese email service run by cloud provider Laxlight.
incidents.impact: The company shut the service down on October 21 shortly after detecting the attack and has not resumed operations.

incidents.victim: DreamHost customers
incidents.vector: An incident impacted DreamHost's FTP/SFTP and webmail services.
incidents.impact: DreamHost reset all customer passwords and blocked accounts until new passwords are set as a precaution.

incidents.victim: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
incidents.vector: The ShinyHunters data-extortion group stole highly sensitive data from FBI systems as part of a broader extortion campaign.
incidents.impact: Investigators are probing executives at two ransomware-negotiation firms suspected of colluding with ShinyHunters, including one accused of helping run the group's victim-pressure website.

incidents.victim: At least seven South Korean financial institutions
incidents.vector: A suspected Chinese-speaking actor (tracked as TAG-217) used the AI-enabled ARTEX penetration-testing framework to breach multiple South Korean financial institutions, testing infrastructure as early as August 2026.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people was exposed; the actor also developed tools to steal cryptocurrency wallet files and expand access to Linux and mobile systems.
